section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS), a 10-item measure proposed by Kroon van Diest and Tylka that assesses perceived restrictive/critical caregiver messages and pressure to eat. It notes that, in US college samples, the scale showed a two-dimensional factor structure (RCM and PEM) and that items are rated on a 5-point frequency scale. No participant-level statistics (sample size, age, race, BMI, correlations) or assessment of body appreciation/BMI are reported here.
section_summary.evidence_source: Full section text: "Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS) ... In US college samples, the authors reported that scores on the scale had a two-dimensional factor structure, consisting of RCM (items 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10) and PEM (items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 9). All items were rated on a 5-point scale (1=Never, 5=Always), with higher scores indicating greater perceived pressure to eat or criticalness/restriction of food choice or intake."
